acqinfo.head: Immediate Source of Acquisition
acqinfo.p: Ford Foundation archive was deposited at the RAC in 2011. Ford Foundation records, correspondence, reports, program files, and officers' papers were transferred to and accessioned by the RAC beginning in 2011. Accessions continue as necessary.
This material was transferred to the RAC in one accession in 2022 and was ingested by the RAC as Accession 2022:058.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The collection contains the office files Mayra Peters-Quintero created and maintained when she worked as a Program Officer at the Ford Foundation. Peters-Quintero managed the Foundation's grants portfolio for Immigrant Rights which became part of the Foundation's Gender, Racial, and Ethnic Justice Program (GREJ). The collection contains one series of Peters-Quintero's subject files.

The collection gives insight into the Ford Foundation's history of immigrant rights related programming from the early 1980s until the establishment of the Immigrant Rights portfolio in GREJ. Throughout these years, the Foundation's programming for immigrants, migrants, and refugees included: immigrant rights and protections; legal representation for immigrants; comprehensive immigration reform; immigration enforcement; immigration integration and civic participation; messaging and media narratives about immigrants and immigration; border security; human security in migration; immigrant employment and the economy; and organization of specific immigration advocates like faith groups, youth, and Latino Americans.

Documents also show how these initiatives responded to contemporary political and social trends regarding immigration in the United States like the backlash against immigrants and concerns about border security after the September 11 Terrorist Attack, the DREAM Act proposal, and the Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA) Act. Other focus areas of the Ford Foundation's human rights programming during this time period like racial justice and LGBT rights are documented in the collection.
Common material formats in the collection include correspondence, memos, reports, strategy documents, notes, drafts, meeting materials, articles, and publications.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This series contains the subject files Mayra Peters-Quintero created and maintained when she served as the Program Officer for the Ford Foundation's grants portfolio on Immigrant Rights. Peters-Quintero's files follow the course of her career at the Foundation and the course of the portfolio's evolution through different Foundation program restructuring phases. Peters-Quintero started managing the portfolio as a Program Officer in the Democracy, Rights, and Justice Program (DRJ), Human Rights when it was called Protecting Immigrant and Migrant Rights. After the Foundation reorganized, it was part of the Gender, Racial, and Ethnic Justice Program (GREJ) as Immigrant Rights. Files in the series contain materials dating from before Peters-Quintero joined the Foundation that document a longer history of programming related to immigrants, migrants and refugees.

The history of the Foundation's immigrant rights programming, broader human rights programming, and program structuring is documented in the series through memos, strategy documents like Line of Work statements and reports, and meeting materials like records from a Trustee Committee trip to the United States-Mexico border.

The series also holds files pertaining to specific grantees and projects. These grantees and projects focused on protecting immigrant rights such as through legal representation, comprehensive immigration reform in the Unites States, grassroots organization for supporting immigrant rights and immigration reform of specific groups like faith and inter-faith groups, immigration enforcement, and public messaging and media narratives about immigrants and immigration.
